clips.text: Whoever wrote this woke to a lantern they didn't light. So did I.
One more print going in than coming out. Something stayed in this house. Maybe that's me.
Bare branches in a shape. I've been telling myself the tree line is only branches, too.
If the hand that waved is the hand that wrote this, whose hand came back to the cabin?
Stay. Finish. Don't go to the lights. Everything on this page wants me standing still.
They burned the candle down so they'd know if they'd been here before. It's burned down, and I don't remember.
The strap said M. Whoever copied it wrote R. Either they read it wrong, or it changed for them.
The blanket's warm on the side I didn't sleep on.
One way out, and the mat's lying perfectly straight, like nobody ever came in.
Somebody sat up with that candle until it went out. Keeping watch, or waiting to be let in.
Any other house would have a back door. This one only goes down.
Count the steps. If there's one more on the way back up, I'm done counting.
Down here the wind's gone. If anything else is breathing, I'll hear it.
No windows. Whatever this house keeps, it keeps down here.
Someone mopped this floor. Someone cleans up after whatever happens here.
A drawer for every one of us. I'm not going to count them.
My own prints are the only thing out here I can trust. So I'll keep counting them.
They've been on since before the snow. Nobody leaves an engine running that long for a stranger.
Standing still is exactly how the pages wanted me. I should move.
Mara. I keep saying it, to hear if it sounds like mine.
I keep watching my right hand, as if it might wave without me.
Three knocks, the page said. I've been waiting for the first one.
If I stop counting my breaths, is anything else keeping count?
Nobody is out here looking for me. Or nobody knows who to look for.
Somewhere, someone wrote down how tall I am. I'd rather they'd written my name.
The road is closed, the lights are on, and I'm the only one still walking toward them.
